where: crates/blaze-item-hash/src/reads.rs Rule::DepCrate, crates/blaze-items/src/goals.rs fact_of_read, hir_def crate_body_owners
what: Turning a body's reads of its own crate's impl and trait tables into facts meant writing the same read-to-fact mapping twice: once in reads.rs for the body store and once in goals.rs for the goal store. A test that walks every body with `crate_body_owners` also never reaches bodies inside a fn body's block, because blocks hold their own items; their reads go untested unless `nameres::demand::body_blocks` is walked as well.
cost: time spent reading both mappings to keep them consistent, and a fixture rewrite once the block bodies turned out to be missing from the walk
cause: two homes for one concept (which fact names a table read); body enumeration split by item tree with no one walk of every body
class: one concept with two homes; an enumeration that silently drops a subset
prevention: reads.rs now delegates every own-crate table read to `Goals.fact_of`, so goals::fact_of_read is the one mapping; a test walks crate_body_owners plus body_blocks owners
fix: fact_of_read maps InherentImpls/TraitImpls/in_crate_trait_value_items/module_items_named/block reads; reads.rs Rule::DepCrate and Rule::Block call it
